questions.reason: An inherited value can be computed during a bottom-up parse when its dependencies are already known. Parent and left-sibling dependencies in an L-attributed definition permit this in suitable cases, using stack values or marker actions. The presence of synthesized attributes alone gives no such guarantee.
questions.note: B is the conventional exam choice supported by GATE Overflow and the linked year-paper review. The wording leaves the evaluation model unspecified. Some non-L-attributed cases can be handled by delaying actions, and L-attribution does not guarantee evaluation during every LR parse. Made Easy keys C, which fails even for an inherited value assigned a constant without synthesized attributes.

questions.reason: Load a into R₁ and c into R₂, then add b and d to their respective registers. SUB e,R₂ yields t₃, SUB R₁,R₂ yields t₄, and MOV R₂,out stores it. Direct generation needs one initial load per independent addition plus the final store.
questions.note: The keys assume direct generation of the stated operations. If the final expression may be rewritten as a+b+c+d−e, one load and one store suffice. GATE Overflow also prints Rⱼ as the register-register destination. Made Easy, the app and the original 2007 scan (p. 13) specify Rᵢ, and the direct MOV count is three for either destination convention.

questions.reason: A is false because L-attributed dependencies permit left-to-right depth-first evaluation. C is false because LR(1) parsing alone does not guarantee that inherited values are available in time for every reduction. Side-effect-free semantic rules define an attribute grammar, and synthesized attributes can be computed at reductions, so B and D are true.
